factual_issues.claim: The ReSeed prototype is an X500-class quadcopter: 22 min endurance, 900 g payload, 1 seed roll.
factual_issues.problem: The 22-minute figure is a planning value without payload, not the flight time while carrying the stated seed load.
factual_issues.evidence: E: `endurance_min: float = 22.0    # hover endurance without payload`; `max_payload_g: float = 900.0`.
factual_issues.fix: ReSeed's X500-class quad model: 22 min without cargo, up to 900 g cargo, 1 seed roll (`reseed/logistics.py` `PROTOTYPE`).

factual_issues.where: C and D / It was tested in SITL first
factual_issues.claim: It was tested in SITL first: a pretend drone inside the computer.
factual_issues.problem: The excerpt instructs users to test in SITL; it does not document that testing actually happened.
factual_issues.evidence: E: "Test in SITL first, fly outdoors or in a netted hall, keep a pilot on the RC transmitter with a kill switch."
factual_issues.fix: Test it in SITL first: a pretend drone inside the computer. Safe and smart!

factual_issues.claim: A servo opens the hatch of the seed roll and hangs under the nose of ReSeed's drone.
factual_issues.problem: Neither this hatch mechanism nor its mounting position is supported by E. The documented release uses a backward jerk. A game-only component should be identified as such.
factual_issues.evidence: E: "before reaching the destination, jerk back so the seeds fly out of the roll".
factual_issues.fix: This game's **servo** sits at the **front**, under the nose. ReSeed's code releases seeds by jerking the drone back.

factual_issues.where: D / Hover over one small patch
factual_issues.claim: Hover over one small patch and drop one seed roll.
factual_issues.problem: The documented mechanism drops seeds from the roll, not the roll itself.
factual_issues.evidence: E: "JERK BACK: reverse to {jerk_speed} m/s for {jerk_s} s - seeds exit the roll".
factual_issues.fix: Hover over one small patch and drop seeds from **one seed roll**. Keep it simple and cheap!

general_cs_errors.where: C and D / Octocopter! Eight rotors
general_cs_errors.claim: An octocopter can still land if one motor fails.
general_cs_errors.problem: Eight rotors do not guarantee a safe motor-out landing. It depends on layout, remaining thrust, load and flight-controller support.
general_cs_errors.fix: Octocopter! Eight rotors share the heavy load. Some can land after one motor fails, but not all.

general_cs_errors.where: C and D / Hexacopter! With six rotors
general_cs_errors.claim: With six rotors, the other five can still bring it down gently.
general_cs_errors.problem: A hexacopter is not automatically capable of a controlled landing after a motor failure.
general_cs_errors.fix: Hexacopter! Six rotors share the load. Some can land after one motor fails, but not all.

general_cs_errors.claim: Carry a medium load, and land safely even if one motor stops.
general_cs_errors.problem: As a mission for choosing a drone by type alone, this implies that rotor count guarantees motor-failure safety. That capability must be established for the particular aircraft.
general_cs_errors.fix: Carry a medium load with six rotors sharing the work.

general_cs_errors.where: C and D / RTL: with no radio
general_cs_errors.claim: With no radio, the drone flies home by itself using GPS.
general_cs_errors.problem: Radio loss does not automatically select RTL on every drone. The failsafe must be configured, and returning requires a usable position estimate and home position.
general_cs_errors.fix: RTL: if set up for this, the drone can use GPS to fly home when the radio link fails. That's a failsafe!

general_cs_errors.where: C and D / VTOL hybrid! It lifts off
general_cs_errors.claim: A VTOL hybrid lifts off like a quad, then tilts into plane mode.
general_cs_errors.problem: Not all hybrid VTOL aircraft tilt to change modes. Some use separate lift and cruise motors; not all have four lift rotors.
general_cs_errors.fix: VTOL hybrid! It takes off straight up, then uses its wings to cruise far like a plane.

general_cs_errors.claim: Four satellites indicate a GPS glitch.
general_cs_errors.problem: Four suitably placed satellites can provide a normal 3D GPS solution. Satellite count alone does not establish a glitch or the reliability of the position.

hard_for_8yo.text: The drone's brain. It reads its gyros, the GPS and the radio receiver, then tells each ESC how fast to spin its motor. A LiPo battery powers it all.
hard_for_8yo.simpler: The drone's brain. It reads motion sensors, **GPS** location and the pilot's radio commands. Each **ESC** motor control sets a motor's speed. A **LiPo** rechargeable battery powers it all.

hard_for_8yo.text: On a Mode 2 transmitter the left stick is throttle (up/down) and yaw (turn). The right stick is pitch (forward/back) and roll (sideways).
hard_for_8yo.simpler: On a **Mode 2** controller—a common layout—the **left stick** controls throttle (up/down) and yaw (turn). The **right stick** controls pitch (forward/back) and roll (sideways).

hard_for_8yo.where: C and D / Make diagonal partners
hard_for_8yo.text: Make diagonal partners spin the same way, and neighbours spin opposite ways.
hard_for_8yo.simpler: Props across from each other spin the same way. Props side by side spin opposite ways.

safety_or_tone.where: C and D / Welcome to Drone Academy
safety_or_tone.problem: For young children, earning 'pilot wings' alongside realistic assembly and flight instructions could suggest readiness to operate a real drone. Establish the game-only boundary.
safety_or_tone.fix: Welcome to Drone Academy! Five lessons earn your game pilot wings. Real flights need a trained adult.

safety_or_tone.where: D / Never fly a puffy LiPo
safety_or_tone.problem: The warning is good, but 'Swap in a good one' directs children to handle a potentially hazardous damaged battery themselves.
safety_or_tone.fix: Never use a puffy LiPo: it can catch fire. Leave it alone and tell an adult.

verdict: A strong game concept, but qualify motor-failure and failsafe claims, distinguish documented ReSeed behavior from game inventions, and add clear adult-supervision boundaries.
